newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nicholas-Applegate buys Credit Lyonnais Asia unit.
newsitem.headline: Nicholas-Applegate buys Credit Lyonnais Asia unit.

text.p: Nicholas-Applegate Capital Management said on Wednesday it has acquired Credit Lyonnais International Asset Management-Asia for an undisclosed price.
Credit Lyonnais Asset Management-Asia (CLIAM-Asia) is the Asia-Pacific asset management division of French bank Credit Lyonnais.
The acquisition, which is subject to regulatory approval, will give Nicholas-Applegate money management operations in Hong Kong, Singapore and London.
The merged firm will be known by the Nicholas-Applegate Capital Management name.

"Becoming part of Nicholas-Applegate will increase the attractiveness of our company as the fund management firm of choice," Paul Mack, managing director of CLIAM-Asia's Hong Kong office, said in a statement.

CLIAM-Asia manages more than US$700 million in assets and advises several single country stock funds that specialise in China, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Indian sub-continent and other countries in Asia.
For periods ending April 1997, CLIAM-Asia's Pacific Growth fund ranked first over the period since its launch in 1988 and the China Growth fund ranked first over the period since its launch in 1992.
Tom Waring, CLIAM-Asia's managing director, will continue to direct the organisation's London, Hong Kong and Singapore offices and will serve as a member of Nicholas-Applegate's management committee.
Mack and Kim Teo will continue to direct the firm's Hong Kong and Singapore offices, respectively.

U.S.-based Nicholas-Applegate is a large institutional and individual fund manager, with US$30 billion under management. Based in San Diego, Nicholas-Applegate describes itself as a premier manager of global stock and bond portfolios.
